Unseasonal rain during flowering or while drying the cherries is a familiar worry. At the MeDili farm, this year's harvest still gives priority to picking ripe cherries and drying them thoroughly, because the quality of a cup of coffee starts with those very days of sun and rain on the farm.

At the MeDili farm, these are days of working out pickers, drying yards and the weather, just like at any other farm. We choose to pick ripe cherries for our Robusta Honey Premium line, because honey processing only gives a lovely sweetness when the cherries are fully ripe. It takes more work, but that is how we keep a cup of Di Linh coffee true to its taste.

Khúc xạ kế đo TDS, tức phần trăm chất ta: A refractometer measures TDS, the percentage of dissolved solids in the cup. Knowing TDS, the beverage weight and the coffee dose, you can calculate EY = TDS × beverage weight ÷ coffee dose. The SCA considers filter coffee to meet the Golden Cup standard at an EY of 18–22% and TDS of 1.15–1.35%. This cup: {1}% × {2}{3}g ÷ {4}{5}g = {6}%.
Khúc xạ kế đo đường và chất tan trong dị: A refractometer measures the sugar and solubles in the pulp juice. The bean receives sucrose from the tree through the vascular system during bean filling, around 130–190 days after flowering in Arabica. The pulp, by contrast, sweetens quickly in roughly the last two months. The two happen in different parts of the cherry, so a high Brix tells you the cherry is ripe but cannot measure the sugar in the bean.
Khúc xạ kế đo độ khúc xạ của dịch thịt q: A refractometer measures the refraction of the pulp juice to estimate solubles, mainly sugar. Brix rises with ripeness, so it's a good tool for choosing the picking day, but it says nothing about the sugar in the bean.

Lượng caffeine phụ thuộc trước hết vào g: The amount of caffeine depends first of all on the variety. According to a comparison sheet from the popular chemistry site Compound Interest, arabica beans contain about 1.2–1.5% caffeine, while robusta beans contain about 2.2–2.7%, nearly double. That is why a strong cup of robusta brewed with a phin usually wakes you up far more than a cup of arabica made with the same amount of ground coffee. Robusta also contains more chlorogenic acids, which contribute to its characteristic bitterness, while arabica has more sugars and fats, so it tastes softer, with a bright acidity.

Lớp da mỏng ngoài cùng, đổi từ xanh sang: The thin outermost skin, turning from green to red as it ripens, holding in water and shielding the flesh inside.
Lớp keo trong, trơn, giàu pectin và đườn: A clear, slippery gel rich in pectin and sugar, clinging tightly to the parchment.
Lớp ngoài cùng mỏng và dai, chuyển từ xa: The outermost layer is thin and tough, turning from green to yellow and then red as it ripens. The skin holds water in the pulp and keeps out insects and mold. When whole cherries are dried, the skin dries into a dark, brittle layer that seals in the bean.
Lớp nhớt chứa đường tự do, pectin, một í: Mucilage contains free sugars, pectin and a little acid and minerals. Sugar is released gradually as the pectin is broken down, so microbes have food for many hours instead of eating it all at once.
Lớp nhớt khô thành màng dính như mật qua: The mucilage dries into a sticky, honey-like film around the parchment. The cup is usually sweet and rounded.
Lớp nhớt là lớp trong suốt, trơn, bám qu: Mucilage is the clear, slippery layer clinging to the parchment, between the fruit pulp and the bean. It is mostly water. Natural giữ nguyên trái nên mẻ bỏ qua tr: Natural keeps the cherries whole, so the batch skips this station. With the skin intact, sugar diffuses more slowly and the yeast needs more time.

Natural giữ nguyên trái, vỏ còn nguyên n: Natural keeps the cherries whole; with the skin intact, sugar diffuses slowly. Honey and Washed are pulped, keeping the mucilage as food for the microbes.
Natural không có bước rửa. Trái phơi mỏn: Natural has no washing step. The cherries are dried in thin layers and turned several times a day so they dry evenly, avoiding trapped moisture that lets contaminant microbes and mold grow.
Natural là phơi nguyên trái, hương trái: Natural means drying the whole cherry; the fruit aromas show differently from lot to lot.
Natural nhiều oxy: phơi mỏng, đảo đều, t: Natural gets plenty of oxygen: dry in thin layers, turn evenly, avoid thick, damp piles.
Natural phơi cả trái chín nên ngọt trái: Natural dries whole ripe cherries, giving ripe-fruit sweetness and full body. Honey removes the skin but keeps the mucilage, for a rounded sweetness. Washed cleans off the mucilage before drying, for a clean cup with bright acidity. Commercial grade dries whole cherries picked ripe and unripe together.

Phần lớn cà phê Indonesia là robusta. US: Most Indonesian coffee is robusta. USDA forecasts robusta at about 10 million bags, down 9.1%. The main cause is too much rain right during flowering and fruit development in the key growing areas of southern Sumatra. Flowers hit by prolonged rain struggle to set fruit and young cherries drop easily, so even though the planted area is unchanged, output still falls short.

A batch with many green cherries, however skillfully roasted, rarely makes a well-rounded cup. In contrast, selectively picking ripe cherries takes more labor, sometimes requiring several picking rounds, but the beans are denser and sweeter and keep the characteristic flavor of their growing area.

But two things are worth noting. First, climate change is making coffee output in many growing areas fluctuate more strongly, so raw material prices will keep swinging erratically over the next few years. Second, when a growing area gets unseasonal rain right at flowering time, not only output but also bean quality suffers: fruit sets unevenly, ripens unevenly, and processing becomes harder.

According to FoodNavigator, many confectionery makers have raised prices several times over the past three years and have very little room left to raise them further. They are looking for ways to cut the amount of cocoa in their recipes, using more substitutes such as carob powder, roasted grains or plant fiber. In other words, the price of a chocolate bar may stay the same, while what is inside may have changed.
Với người uống, giai đoạn giá nhân thấp: For coffee drinkers, a period of low green coffee prices is actually the time to pay more attention to quality than to price. When prices fall, pressure to cut costs in picking and drying may increase. Beans mixed with many unripe cherries or dried in a hurry easily make a cup harsh and astringent, lacking a sweet aftertaste. On the other hand, carefully sorted beans dried in enough sun give a rich yet smooth taste. So instead of asking only about price, you should also ask: where the beans were grown, how they were picked and processed, and when they were roasted.

“Sẻ” là tên dân gian, không phải tên phâ: “Sẻ” (“sparrow”) is a folk name, not an official classification. Cà Sẻ, Robusta Sẻ, Ro Sẻ and small-bean Robusta all refer to the Robusta brought to Vietnam in the early 20th century and widely grown in the Central Highlands before the selected varieties of the WASI institute. The trees are propagated from seed, so the population is uneven: each tree has its own shape, cherries and yield. The name reflects the small beans, small cherries and compact canopy.

“Sẻ” is a folk name, not an official classification; the general name is still Robusta. Cà Sẻ, Robusta Sẻ, Ro Sẻ and small-bean Robusta all refer to the old Robusta variety (Origin Robusta) that the French brought to Vietnam in the early 20th century and took up to Di Linh and across the Central Highlands to plant, before the selected varieties of the WASI institute existed. The trees are propagated from seed, so the population is uneven: each tree has its own shape, cherries and yield. The name reflects the small beans, small cherries and compact canopy.
